item.title: nixos/duckdns: verify TLS certificates
item.description:
Fixes #584693

Drop -k from the curl call so the token is only sent over a verified TLS connection. Checked that duckdns.org's certificate verifies with plain curl.

Tested with a NixOS VM test (aarch64-linux VMs on an aarch64-darwin host): a fake www.duckdns.org over HTTPS with a private test CA. Test + module files, run with nix-build test.nix.

  • this PR, CA trusted: update succeeds
  • this PR, CA not trusted: refused with curl: (60), token not sent
  • before this PR (-k), CA not trusted: update succeeds, so the token goes to the impostor

The change and the test were prepared with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) and reviewed , tested by me.

item.title: [26.05] systemd: 260.5 -> 260.7
item.description:
This PR picks up the security-relevant stable backports shared with 262.2, among them:

  • nsresourced filesystem restrictions
  • portabled extension image authentication
  • polkit action fixes in machined and importd
  • a one-byte overflow in logind
  • journal hash chain loop detection.

I regenerated the patches per the instructions in default.nix. Patch 0005 conflicted with the backported version of @nikstur's patch "taint: don't taint if /bin, /usr/sbin, /var/run don't exist"; it now matches the unstable version. We would have run into this if we put v260.6 into 26.05, but we didn't.

Changelog: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/compare/v260.5...v260.7

It's not cherry-picked because unstable is already on systemd v262. Previous PRs were similar.

  • #558350
  • #563830

I'm hoping to get this in so that 26.05 is put out to pasture in a good state.

item.title: [26.05] python3Packages.openusd: 25.05.01 -> 26.11.1
item.description:
Backport of #583758. Part of #583070.

Updates OpenUSD on release-26.05 from 25.05.01 to 26.11.1, using the same package expression as master. This fixes CVE-2026-92211 / GHSA-75r4-2rhh-hrxw (double free in CrateFile::_ReadPathsImpl for crate files older than 0.4.0) and the other OpenUSD advisories fixed since 25.05.01: GHSA-58p5-r2f6-g2cj, GHSA-grjp-54v3-c442, GHSA-q75h-g2h7-fgxg, GHSA-8878-wr6v-j5cm, GHSA-qgc5-vc49-x7jw and GHSA-5hf7-7jmm-gqcf (command injection in usdview / usdedit). GHSA-8wwg-27mq-f669 concerns libaom, which 25.05.01 bundles in its AVIF plugin; 26.11.1 picks up upstream's fix.

Why a version bump instead of patches: the CVE fix's behaviour change (crate files < 0.4.0 are rejected) applies either way, and backporting every advisory to 25.05.01 would mean carrying several hand-adapted patches. The previous stable update attempts didn't fail on reverse dependencies: #435178 was reverted in 87b82df76136 because openusd itself failed to build, and #497691 landed on master after the 26.05 branch-off.

Changelog: https://github.com/PixarAnimationStudios/OpenUSD/blob/v26.11.1/CHANGELOG.md

Commits:

  • python3Packages.openusd: 25.05.01 -> 26.11.1: the expression from master. Compared to 25.05.01, the embree 4 patch is upstream now and dropped, so is the distutils dependency; the OpenImageIO plugin is enabled (required by sdrOsl since 26.11); PXR_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR is set; and a pxrConfig.cmake patch plus propagated openimageio/embree keep find_package(pxr) working for consumers such as f3d.
  • blender: fix build with openusd 26.11: same fix as on master (unused glf/drawTarget.h include removed upstream).
  • vtk_9_6: fix build: backport of #571724 and its follow-up #572295, squashed so that no intermediate commit breaks vtk 9.5. vtk_9_6 links against openusd and otherwise clashes with openusd's exported pegtl target. Unlike master, postPatch is null (not "") for vtk < 9.6: vtk 9.5 had no postPatch on release-26.05, so an empty string would still change its derivation and rebuild everything depending on the default vtk.

Testing:

  • x86_64-linux: see #583758 (nixpkgs-review: 11 built, 0 failed; Kitchen_set loads, renders with usdrecord, opens in usdview).
  • aarch64-linux: nixpkgs-review on this branch (b6cdd316), 9 built, 1 failed. blendfarm fails in configureNuget, before anything touching openusd is built, with System.IO.IOException: ... 'NuGet-Migrations' from System.Threading.Mutex. That comes from the review environment (a Kubernetes pod without the Nix sandbox). blendfarm built fine in the sandboxed x86_64 review of #583758.

item.title: hentai-at-home: 1.6.5 -> 1.6.6
item.description:
https://forums.e-hentai.org/index.php?showtopic=234458

1.6.6 [SECURITY, IMPORTANT] - 2026-11-05

  • Corrected a missing directory-traversal check in the H@H Gallery Downloader code that could potentially have allowed the server to tell the client to overwrite any file that was write-accessible for the user H@H was running as with an arbitrary file, by injecting a file path as a filename in the gallery meta file. This breaks the fundamental H@H security principle where the server is never supposed to be able to tell the client to do anything dangerous.

Under some hypothetical and unlikely circumstances, this could have been leveraged by a MitM to do the same thing. Specifically, a malicious party would have had to be in a position to intercept and alter data received from the server, and the client's owner must have actively requested a gallery download via the site at the same time.

There was no way for a MitM to activate the download mechanism independently, as there is no way to start the downloader unless the server explicitly sends a "start the downloader" command to the client - this command cannot be forged unless the client's secret key has been leaked. There are no indicators that this has ever been exploited.

While the activation of the H@H Downloader mechanism has been disabled server-side for any client running versions prior to this update, the potential for the server to activate and exploit this mechanism remains until the client is updated. As such, we recommend updating as soon as possible, even if you do not use the H@H Downloader.

Due to the security implications, this update will be made mandatory unless any issues are discovered shortly after release.

Thanks to oOoEstheiM for privately reporting this issue.

  • Added a signature to RPC responses to detect and reject alterations in general. (This prevents a MitM from interfering with other client operations, but is considered hardening, as it was found to have no significant security impact since H@H was designed not to trust the server in the first place.)

  • Added a signature to the gallery downloader meta files to detect and reject altered file lists.

  • Added additional hardening to ensure that filenames and filetypes provided to the downloader can only correspond to those that are allowed in the gallery system.

  • Since the file hash is not always known when requesting resampled images via the H@H Downloader, and these requests are not latency-sensitive, these file downloads now always use HTTPS. Note that this is not necessary elsewhere, since the hash is otherwise always known, and the file can therefore be verified regardless of transport.

  • If we bail out on startup because the available disk space is less than the assigned cache size, we now explicitly print both the required and actual available space.

  • The client will now properly handle the FAIL_STARTUP_LOOP and FAIL_UNSUPPORTED_LOCATION startup codes, instead of failing back to re-request the ID and key.

item.title: hdf5_2: make default version
item.description:
This an attempt to closes https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/583060

  • promote hdf5_2 to the default version
  • keep hdf5_1_14 for now (can most likely be removed).
  • clean up the szipSupport flag. We can always build with szip support. The original has an unfree license, but the newer replacement, libaec, has a BSD license.
  • basing it on master for now to make testing more convenient. Should probably go into staging.

The update seems to work well:

  • gdal , qgis still build @imincik.
  • major python packages such as h5py and pandas is still build.
  • scientific software are such as cp2k, openmolcas, and petsc still build.

Purpose of this draft PR is collect feedback. Once we have consensus, I will rebase it onto staging, and we can move forward.

item.title: surrealdb: 3.0.0 -> 3.3.5; surrealdb-surrealkv: 3.0.0 -> 4.0.0
item.description:
<status: not ready to merge until rocksdb 11.8.x available, see #576026>

As part of the 4.0.0 release, upstream has removed alternative on-disk storage engines such as rocksdb [1]. surrealdb 4 will automatically convert underlying data store. However, the better option is to allow nixpkgs users to update to latest 3.x version (and resolve identified security issues). Then users can upgrade to 4.x on their own time schedule.

  • diffs: https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb/compare/v3.0.0...v3.3.5 https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb/compare/v3.0.0...v4.0.0

[1] https://surrealdb.com/releases/4.0#4-0-0--one-storage-engine-from-server-to-browser
